SMTO-GML-0013 — This Gmail change needs your approval first

GUID: 8038d5f7-ee70-4980-a763-2106fc8107ec
Slug: gmail-confirmation-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO was about to change your mailbox, but it didn't have your approval for this change, so it stopped. Nothing in your mailbox was changed by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again in a conversation you are watching, so it can show you its approval request. Changes to your mailbox only go ahead after someone approves them, and a task nobody is watching can't get that approval.
  2. When the approval card appears, read the planned change, and for bulk changes check the list of emails, then select Approve once. Approving the exact change you see is what allows SMTO to make it.
  3. If you didn't mean to make this change, select Deny / stop task instead. Nothing has been changed yet, so stopping is safe.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the email change as done after you approve it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, especially if no approval card appears when you ask in a conversation. Don't change SMTO's approval settings just to get past this message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail write tool ran without an approval in its execution context and without full-access permission, or GmailService.batch_modify_messages was called without confirm=True.

What this means

  • The mutation capability lacks applicable confirmation/full-access policy, or batch modification is invoked without its required confirm flag. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The mutation capability lacks applicable confirmation/full-access policy, or batch modification is invoked without its required confirm flag.

How to diagnose it

  • Review exact account, operation and previewed selection under the current approval policy.

How to fix it

  • NativeGmailCapability.execute requires execution_context.confirmation or approval_full_access_enabled() for mutation tools; GmailService.batch_modify_messages also requires confirm=True. Run the request through a path that raises the normal approval prompt (or a permission policy that allows it), and for bulk changes confirm the current gmail.preview_modify result.
  • Review the exact current preview and explicitly confirm the intended mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended mutation is authorized through its supported confirmation flow.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
